# What the release workflow installs to read the bill of materials a second
# time - spdx-tools, the SPDX project's own validator, and everything it
# imports. ADR116, the decisions taken at the README.
#
# Every package is pinned to a version AND to the bytes of its file, and pip is
# run with --require-hashes, so it refuses a package this list does not name, a
# version that is not this one and a file whose bytes are not these. This runs
# in the job whose output the release attests, so what it installs is held the
# way the actions are: to exactly what was read, never to a name.
#
# Wheels only, never a source archive, because building one runs its setup
# code. PyYAML is the one package with compiled code in it, so it carries a
# wheel for each of Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 on x86_64 Linux. ubuntu-latest
# has 3.12 today. A runner with a Python outside these fails at the install,
# loudly, and builds nothing.
#
# Resolved 2026-11-02 in python:3.12-slim from spdx-tools==0.8.5, with the
# hashes and the licences read from https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json
# the same day. Nothing here reaches a user - it runs beside the build and is
# never part of it - so the licences are recorded rather than sieved.

# Apache-2.0 - the validator, LICENSE read at the v0.8.5 tag

    --hash=sha256:7c2d5865941be9d2e898f5b084e8d5422dd298dc5a29320ddb198fec304f59c4
